title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-20261017 登顶 Code Arena: WebDev 开源模型榜首
content:
Arena.ai· @arena · X·· 3 小时前精选AI 评分69
AI 导读
Arena 宣布 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-20261017 (Max) 成为 Code Arena: WebDev 榜单第一开源模型，超过 Kimi K3 (Max)，成本低约 10 倍。
推荐理由
Arena 榜单给出了具体排名、分数和价格点，读者可以据此评估 DeepSeek 新版模型在 WebDev 编码上的性价比位置。
正文 · AI 翻译
激动人心的消息：@deepseek_ai 的 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-20261017 (Max) 现已成为 Code Arena: WebDev 中排名第一的开源模型，以低 10 倍的成本超越 Kimi K3 (Max)！
亮点：
- 排名第一的开源模型，领先于 Kimi K3 (Max)
- 以 1670 分位列总榜第 12，领先于 Claude Opus 5 (High)，与 GPT-6 Sol (Max) 相差约 10 分以内
- 以每百万输入/输出 token $0.3/$1.2 的价格推动帕累托前沿移动
- 相比上一版 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-20260910 提升 52 分
祝贺 @deepseek_ai 团队为开源生态又做出了一项强有力的贡献！
来源：Arena.ai · x.com

report.summary: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-20261017 (Max) becomes Code Arena: WebDev's top open-source model, beating Kimi K3 (Max) at roughly one-tenth the cost.
report.background: Coding ability has become the main competitive battleground for frontier AI models, since developers are the highest-value and fastest-paying user segment. Code Arena: WebDev, run by Arena.ai, scores models through head-to-head comparisons on real web development tasks rather than static test sets, making it a widely watched signal for practical coding quality. Chinese labs in particular have been competing on price-performance: DeepSeek, Moonshot's Kimi line and others release frequent point updates, each trying to land on the cost-quality 'Pareto frontier' — the set of models where nothing is both better and cheaper. The previous DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-20260910 was already competitive, and this October build is positioned as a fast iteration rather than a generational jump, which is why the headline number is cost, not just score.
key_points: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-20261017 (Max) ranks first among open-source models in Code Arena: WebDev, ahead of Kimi K3 (Max). On the overall leaderboard it sits 12th with 1,670 points — above Claude Opus 5 (High) and within about 10 points of GPT-6 Sol (Max).

Pricing is the headline: $0.30 per million input tokens and $1.20 per million output tokens, roughly one-tenth the cost of Kimi K3 (Max). Arena frames this as a shift of the Pareto frontier — near-frontier coding quality at a fraction of the price.

The model scored 52 points higher than the previous build, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-20260910. That is a large jump for a point release, suggesting rapid iteration cycles and heavy emphasis on coding and web-development data.

Arena's ranking comes from pairwise comparisons on real web development tasks, which reflects hands-on usefulness better than static benchmarks. However, arena votes measure preference, not verified correctness, so results should be checked against your own evaluation before production adoption.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the message is that price, not just capability, is now the main competition. An open-weight model that nearly matches closed frontier systems at one-tenth the cost puts pressure on closed-model pricing and strengthens the case for self-hosting. For developers, cheaper tokens mean coding agents can run longer, retry more, and be deployed in high-volume pipelines where frontier pricing was previously prohibitive; the trade-off is that arena scores do not guarantee correctness, so teams still need their own task-specific evaluations. For regular users, the practical effect is cheaper AI coding assistants and IDE tools, plus faster feature turnover as vendors pass savings and new versions downstream.
report.tools: Follow the Code Arena: WebDev leaderboard on Arena.ai for live rankings and pricing. Try DeepSeek's API or open-weight releases directly, and compare against Kimi K3 on the same tasks. OpenRouter and similar gateways let you switch between models with one key. For hands-on coding agent testing, pair these models with open-source agents such as Cline, Aider or OpenHands, and validate results against your own repo-level test suite rather than relying on arena scores alone.
